ModMetaData.name: Neat Edges
ModMetaData.author: MrBeverage
ModMetaData.description:
Stop soil and water washing a ragged fringe across your floors.
RimWorld fades every terrain one tile into whatever it touches, and the receiving tile gets no say in it. That is why a clean stone terrace meeting open ground always looks like it is dissolving at the rim. Bridges are the one thing in the game that escape it, and only because they are bridges.
Neat Edges gives you that clean line anywhere, from the Floors tab of the Architect menu.
· Hard edge: an invisible marker. Pick a side by rotating, and stack them on one tile for any combination. · Hard edge area: whole tiles, every edge at once, painted by dragging the way you paint a home area. Free and instant, and nothing is drawn on the map. · Floor borders: visible trim in wood, stone or metal that takes paint, as a straight strip, a corner, or a runner down both sides of a corridor. Each hardens the edges it covers. · Corners close themselves. Where two hardened edges meet, the corner between them is sealed too, and a run ends crisply instead of the fringe curling around its last tile. · The marker costs no materials, since it changes how an edge draws and nothing else. · An overlay toggle on the bottom-right row shows every marker and the painted area, because an invisible thing you cannot find is an invisible thing you cannot remove.
Coming from Perspective: Paths? Remove it and load your save: the areas you painted with it load as the hard edge area. The painted area follows Owlchemist's Perspective: Paths, which solved the whole-tile case first.
You can add it to a running save. Removing it drops the markers, the trims and the painted area, with an error logged for each missing type on the next load; your floors and terrain are untouched.
Works with any floor from any mod, and with vanilla bridges alongside.
